newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa weighs future savings fund rules - Ramos.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa weighs future savings fund rules - Ramos.

text.p: South Africa's Finance Ministry is discussing measures with the Financial Services Board to protect savings after the abolition of foreign exchange controls, a senior official said on Wednesday.
Finance director general Maria Ramos said measures also needed to be in place before the completion of the gradual lifting of exchange controls to guard against money laundering.

"It's all about putting checks and balances into the system to ensure that at the end of the day...you have also been able to maintain the integrity of the financial system. That's the approach we are taking to exchange control," she told reporters.
"We have to manage the process in a way so as to ensure that at the end of the day we don't create unnecessary instability in the financial system."

Expanding on comments by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel on Tuesday saying that the country's savings would have to be protected from the effects of exchange control abolition, she said institutions might be subject to prudential rules.
"We're working with the Financial Services Board, which represents the industry, and we will work closely with the industry. The objective is to ensure the integrity of portfolios," she said.

Pointing to rules in other countries setting a 10 to 20 percent limit on pension fund investments abroad, Ramos said pension and savings institutions needed to be certain that they could meet their rand liabilities.

"We may need some very broad guidelines on what those prudential requirements should be so that insurance companies and pension funds and the finacial systems in general maintain their integrity," she said.
South Africa already allows investment funds to invest up to 10 percent of new funds abroad.
Ramos said the proposed prudential requirements should not be seen as foreign exchange controls.
